newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent, North Sea grades gain ground.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent, North Sea grades gain ground.

text.p: Cash Brent outright and intermonth spread prices firmed a little on Friday, boosted by the sharp draw in U.S. crude stocks reported on Thursday.
North Sea benchmark Dated Brent stabilised after losing ground versus paper in a lower sale on Christmas Eve and other North Sea grades also firmed a touch.
Intermonth spread talk saw Feb/Mar Brent add a few cents to +47/50 cents, recovering some of the losses posted in New York on Thursday. Jan/Feb moved to +32/35 cents.
February Brent was 16 cents higher on the IPE at $23.55 a barrel after the U.S. EIA estimated national crude stocks had fallen 6.1 million barrels and the API showed a 5.15 million barrel crude draw.

Dealers said Dated Brent for Jan 10-12 was offered at Jan Brent -20 cents on Friday, bid at Jan -27 cents after trading on Tuesday at Jan -27 cents. That compared with a previous sale at Jan -10 cents on Monday.
Four of five Brent dates were kept on Tuesday, two by the company which concluded the lower sale. A fifth was clocked to a U.S. bank.
"We'd expect to get better than the last done," said a seller.
Despite an open U.S. arbitrage dealers said interest from U.S. buyers remained poor.
CFDs for next week, reflecting the weaker sentiment, slipped to Feb +10/15 cents, down 10 cents from Tuesday. Weeks further forward were down five cents.
Other North Sea grades were sparsely talked but showing signs of improvement. Ekofisk for Jan 20 moved at Dated Brent plus 30 cents from a pre-Christmas sale at +26 cents.
